segmentation.text: the drivers of all other vehicles
to the vehicle about to enter or cross the through highway

elements.justification: 'Said driver' is the driver subsection (A) addresses: the driver of a vehicle (the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) at an entrance to the through highway, which DEF-NRS-484A-275 describes as one where 'vehicular traffic from intersecting highways is required by law to yield right-of-way to vehicles on such through highway in obedience to either an authorized stop sign or a yield sign, or other official traffic-control device'. Read: o occupies (rel.occupies) a carrier c2 (st.travel_region) with st.lane_enters(c2, j) for the intersection j the subject approaches, c2 governed (dev.governs) by a stop sign, a yield sign or a traffic signal showing flashing_red. dev.governs 'Not a stand-in for: a position' does not apply: governance is read. The role 'driver' is read through o's controlled motion, never as membership.

'having so yielded' requires the act itself, with its qualifications: o yielded right-of-way 'to vehicles on such through highway in obedience to' the device at its entrance (DEF-NRS-484A-275). Read over o's approach, from the last observation at which o's occupancy of c2 rose until its occupancy of j rose: where c2 is governed by a stop sign or flashing-red signal, o came to rest on c2 short of j (drv.motion.complete_halt, 'complete cessation from movement'); and o did not proceed (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) while a vehicle on the through highway was in a danger of a crash with it, the right-of-way bound operationalized on s9 (prim.closest_approach_within / prim.closest_approach_distance with p.conflict_horizon and p.conflict_centre_clearance), nor touched one (rel.contact). The primitives' exclusion 'alone establishes none of [contact, clearance, danger]' is respected: the danger is the operationalization's bound. Subsection (A) itself is not in this plan nor accepted, so its words are carried by these observables, not by composition.

'vehicles' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id'. Its exclusion 'a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle — never membership' does not apply: 'the drivers of' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency reading), and the aggregate only states the class. 'all other' = every vehicle other than the one about to enter: the subject is never the same road user as o.

st.lane_enters: 'a road user's approach to an intersection is a carrier it occupies (rel.occupies) whose entrance end is that intersection ... approaches through it whatever its motion'. The carrier c is quantified over st.travel_region (the abstract union of the carrier kinds lane_enters admits) and the intersection j over st.intersection ('the region where two roadways meet'). Not a stand-in for the subject's presence in the intersection or for dev.governs: the relation read is entry topology, as its contract states.

DEF-NRS-484A-275: a through highway is one 'at the entrances to which vehicular traffic from intersecting highways is required by law to yield right-of-way to vehicles on such through highway in obedience to either an authorized stop sign or a yield sign, or other official traffic-control device'. Read on the devices: the subject's approach carrier c is governed (dev.governs: 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') by no stop sign ('regulatory sign requiring a full halt'), yield sign ('regulatory sign requiring yielding without a mandatory halt') or traffic signal showing flashing_red, while the entering vehicle's carrier c2 into the same j is governed by one of them. dev.governs 'Not a stand-in for: a position' does not apply: governance, not a halting place, is read.

To yield is to grant the other precedence: the subject does not proceed in conflict with it. kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' tells a subject still proceeding from one that has given way; rel.contact 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)' marks precedence taken outright. rel.contact's exclusion 'a near miss' is respected: the near-conflict is bounded by the operationalization of s9, not by contact.

'the vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle (ru.aggregate, as on s5). 'about to enter or cross the through highway' is an imminent movement, read by the movement it leads to: o, coming from carrier c2 with st.lane_enters(c2, j), occupies j (rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (... intersection ...)') now or at an observation within p.conflict_horizon ahead; j is the intersection of the through highway the subject approaches (st.intersection).

operationalizations.standard: right-of-way: DEF-NRS-484A-210 'approaching under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence to the other'
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: a danger of a crash exists where, under constant velocities, the centres of the two road users come within a centre clearance comparable to their half-extents inside a time-to-collision horizon; a road user whose speed is at or below the source's speed resolution has granted precedence

residues.why: a permission granted to the entering driver; it imposes no condition on the through-highway drivers beyond the entering vehicle's movement, which s10 carries, so the duty is the same whether or not the permission is read

applicability: The subject, a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), occupies a carrier c (st.travel_region) with st.lane_enters(c, j) for an intersection j (st.intersection), and c is governed (dev.governs) by no stop sign, no yield sign and no traffic signal showing flashing_red; and some road user o, not the subject, is a vehicle (same aggregate) that came from a carrier c2 with st.lane_enters(c2, j) governed by a stop sign, a yield sign or a traffic signal showing flashing_red, and either occupies j (having occupied c2 or j at every observation since it last occupied c2) or occupies c2 and occupies j at some observation within p.conflict_horizon ahead; and o has so yielded: since the last observation at which o's occupancy of c2 rose, (i) where c2 is governed by a stop sign or a flashing-red signal, drv.motion.complete_halt(o; p.halt_speed_tolerance) held at some observation at which o occupied c2 and not j, and (ii) at every observation before o's occupancy of j rose, it is not the case that o's kin.speed exceeded p.halt_speed_tolerance while, for some vehicle v other than o that occupied j or a carrier entering j governed by no stop sign, yield sign or flashing-red signal, prim.closest_approach_within(o, v; p.conflict_horizon) held with prim.closest_approach_distance(o, v; p.conflict_horizon) below p.conflict_centre_clearance, and o was in rel.contact with no such v; this is unknown where o's occupancy of c2 rose before the recording began.
obligation: For every road user o selected as in the applicability (re-bound with the whole selection: a vehicle other than the subject, from a carrier c2 entering the same j governed by a stop sign, yield sign or flashing-red signal, entering j within p.conflict_horizon or already in j having come from c2, and having so yielded as the applicability states): it is not the case that the subject's kin.speed exceeds p.halt_speed_tolerance while prim.closest_approach_within(subject, o; p.conflict_horizon) holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, o; p.conflict_horizon) below p.conflict_centre_clearance; and rel.contact(subject, o) does not hold.

narrowings.why: 'drivers' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle approaching on the through highway, whoever or whatever controls it

the legal designation 'through highway' is read through the devices on the road that display it: a stop sign, a yield sign or a flashing-red signal governing the entering approach and none governing the subject's approach; 'other official traffic-control device' is read as the flashing-red signal, the remaining device that requires traffic from the intersecting highway to halt and yield
'about to enter or cross' is an imminent movement, read by the entry into the intersection it leads to (within p.conflict_horizon ahead) or by the vehicle already crossing

precedence is read as the subject not proceeding (speed above the halt tolerance) while a constant-velocity closest approach to the entering vehicle falls below the centre clearance within the horizon, and never touching it; how the subject gives way (slowing or halting) is not modelled

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Subject vehicle on a lane entering j with no device; o halts at the stop sign on the cross approach and starts into j when no through vehicle is within the conflict bound; the subject then arrives and the subject keeps its speed and the constant-velocity closest approach of centres is below p.conflict_centre_clearance within p.conflict_horizon.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same scene; the subject brakes to a halt short of j while o crosses; while the closest approach is below the clearance the subject's speed is at or below p.halt_speed_tolerance, and no contact occurs.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject approaches j on the through approach, but no vehicle is on or entering from a stop-sign or yield-sign approach of j.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the source does not observe which carriers the stop sign governs, so whether o's approach is an entrance to a through highway is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: All-way stop: the subject's own carrier is governed by a stop sign, so it is not on a through highway.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, except that o never comes to rest at its stop sign before entering j: it has not so yielded, and the duty does not arise.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, except that o halts and then pulls into j while the subject is already within the conflict bound of it: o has not so yielded.

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: Hayward (1972) time-to-collision; Swedish Traffic Conflict Technique (Hydén 1987)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: passenger-car dimensions (AASHTO design vehicle P: 5.8 m by 2.1 m)

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed noise floor of vehicle odometry and tracked-object estimates
